messages:
ashley-cs: Hey team, incoming escalation from AcmeApp — they rotated their API key at 09:00 UTC and now CI-deployed jobs are getting 401s. Production traffic (manual deploys) looks fine. Any ideas?

maria-support: Can you paste the customer error snippet and which endpoint is failing?

ashley-cs: Error from their CI run (snippet):
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"apikey invalid or revoked","code":401}
```
Happens during the automated integration test stage that hits our /v1/generate endpoint.

kevin-customer: Confirming — we rotated via our Vault UI and updated the Vault secret. Local retry works for us, but CI runs still fail until we re-run pipeline.

jake-ops: Sounds like the CI runner has a cached env var or a long-lived secret injected at agent start. Which CI are they using?

kevin-customer: They use self-hosted GitLab runners (k8s). They set the variable in GitLab project settings.

eli-platform: Two common failure modes: 1) CI runners started before the secret change still have the old env injected into running pods/agents; 2) the pipeline uses a cached image with baked-in secret (bad practice).

maria-support: Ashley — can you ask for these quick checks from the customer: `kubectl get pods -n gitlab-runner -o jsonpath="{.items[*].metadata.annotations}"` and confirm runner pod restart time? Also ask if they use Vault Agent injector or the GitLab variable mask.

ashley-cs: Sent the ask. Customer replied: runner pods uptime 5d, they rotate secrets nightly, but this key rotation was manual. They also have `gitlab-runner` deployed as a Deployment (no DaemonSet).

jake-ops: If runner pods are long-lived, env vars set in GitLab will only propagate to new jobs; existing runner processes will keep the old env. Restarting the runner deployment should pick up new variables.

kevin-customer: We restarted the runner pods and retried — CI jobs pass now. So root cause = runner process env not updated.

eli-platform: For long-term: recommend one of 2 patterns: 
1) Use Vault dynamic secrets / short-lived tokens via AppRole so CI fetches fresh creds at job start.
2) Add a webhook to restart runners or use ephemeral runners per job.

maria-support: Also recommend removing any baked secrets from images and rotate the key again now that they restarted. Confirmed fix: restart+rerun worked.

ashley-cs: Logged resolution with customer. They want a checklist to avoid future incidents.

jake-ops: I'll draft a short runbook:
- Verify how CI injects secrets (env var vs vault injector)
- If self-hosted runners, include a step to restart runners after secret rotate
- Prefer short-lived credentials and rotate via automation
- Search repo images for hardcoded keys: `grep -R "REDWOOD_API_KEY" .`

eli-platform: Bonus safety: add a CI job that validates current runner env on startup: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/status || exit 1` — will fail the job if key invalid.

deploy-bot: [deploy] pipeline 4321 failed (401) -> retried after runner restart -> success :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: Incident closed. Root cause: self-hosted runner env not refreshed after secret rotation. Remediation: restart runners, consider short-lived secrets.

maria-support: Adding follow-up task: provide customer with short how-to for GitLab runner restart and recommended Vault integration links. Assigning to @jake-ops. :thumbsup:

ashley-cs: Thanks all — customer is happy. Closing thread.
